rule.TRUE_PRODUCTION: production code; the object is created, caller-owned (row), never disposed on some path, and the leak is real for the program
rule.TRUE_TEST_SAMPLE: the same in test, sample or documentation code
rule.BENIGN: the object is caller-owned but its lifetime is the process lifetime by design (a singleton created once at startup) or it is disposed by a convention the code follows elsewhere
rule.FALSE: the object is disposed, escapes into a field/return/collection, or the row does not apply on that path (analysis error)
rule.UNDECIDABLE: cannot be decided from the source

overlap_rule.OWN_NET_ONLY: no other tool flags the line

overlap_rule.EXISTING_TOOL_WITH_MANUAL_MODEL: another tool would need a hand-written model of the callable
overlap_rule.UNKNOWN: the tool could not be run on the project

findings.row_class: rederived_same_source (Npgsql 10.0.3 source derivation, E1; net10.0 asset re-pin)
findings.reason: DbConnector.GetDbConnection (library code, DatabaseInterpreter.Core): for every connection request a NEW NpgsqlDataSourceBuilder(...).Build() data source is created, a connection is taken from it and returned, and the data source itself is dropped; each NpgsqlDataSource owns its own connection pool, so pools (and their open connections) accumulate for the process lifetime; Npgsql documents the data source as a create-once object. Real resource leak in production code; severity: unbounded pool growth under repeated use
findings.overlap_evidence: IDisposableAnalyzers (54 warnings in the project) flags DbConnector.cs:59 (factory.CreateConnection()) but not line 50 (dataSourceBuilder.Build() whose result is only used as the receiver of the returned CreateConnection()); CA2000 silent

findings.message: IDisposable local 'multiHost' is never disposed (leak) [resource: disposable]
findings.row_class: rederived_same_source (Npgsql 10.0.3 source derivation, E1; net10.0 asset re-pin)
findings.reason: Builder.BuildMainDataSource: var multiHost = new NpgsqlDataSourceBuilder(cs).BuildMultiHost(); return multiHost.WithTargetSession(target); -- the returned object is Npgsql's MultiHostDataSourceWrapper (cached per target inside the multi-host source; OwnsConnectors => false, no Dispose override), so the caller's 'await using var dataSource = builder.BuildMainDataSource(...)' (Program.cs:496) disposes the wrapper and never the wrapped multi-host pool: the verdict is semantically correct (nothing ever disposes multiHost), but BuildMainDataSource runs once at startup and the pool lives for the process; would become a real leak only if the method were called repeatedly
findings.overlap_evidence: IDisposableAnalyzers flags Builder.cs:3088 (another BuildMultiHost site) and 318/319 (Serilog), not 3250; CA2000 silent at 3250
